questions.q: Which Snowflake role does this lesson connect Power BI with, and why?
options: DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST — the read-only role meant for exactly this, matching the Advanced capstone's own least-privilege RBAC
DRIFTWOOD_TRANSFORMER, since it has the broadest access
ACCOUNTADMIN, to avoid any permission issues
DRIFTWOOD_COMPLIANCE, since it can see unmasked data
questions.explain: DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST is the read-only role for human analysts and Power BI, consistent with the Advanced capstone's least-privilege RBAC design.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between Import and DirectQuery mode?
options: Import pulls a snapshot into Power BI's own model on a refresh schedule; DirectQuery queries the source live on every visual render
Import only works with CSV files, never with Snowflake
DirectQuery is always faster than Import regardless of pipeline design
There is no real difference — they produce identical performance
questions.explain: Import snapshots data on a schedule; DirectQuery sends a live query to the source on every render, which is slower and more expensive on the warehouse.

questions.q: Why does this lesson choose Import mode for this project specifically?
options: The pipeline already refreshes every 5 minutes via Tasks, so a 15-30 minute Import refresh gives data current enough for weekly reporting without hitting the warehouse on every page load
DirectQuery is not supported by the Snowflake connector at all
Import is required whenever a VARIANT column exists anywhere upstream
Finance specifically requested DirectQuery and Support specifically requested Import
questions.explain: Given the Tasks already keep data current every 5 minutes, Import with a modest refresh schedule is the better fit than querying Snowflake live on every render.

questions.q: What warehouse does this lesson's Power BI connection use?
options: DRIFTWOOD_WH, the same warehouse this chapter's Tasks already use
A brand-new warehouse created specifically for Power BI
No warehouse is needed for a read-only connection
The ACCOUNTADMIN default warehouse
questions.explain: The lesson reuses DRIFTWOOD_WH, the same warehouse already powering the pipeline's Tasks.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend spot-checking both imported tables before building any report pages?
options: Catching a connection or import mistake with flat tables and no visuals yet is far simpler than noticing something's off once two full pages are built
Power BI automatically deletes any table that isn't checked within 24 hours
Spot-checking is required by Snowflake's terms of service
It isn't actually necessary — this is just an optional suggestion with no real reasoning given
questions.explain: A simple sanity check against the Lesson 8 baseline numbers catches problems early, before they're buried under two fully-built report pages.
